title: The moment that defines you
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What is the moment that most defines you?
I asked each person: give me the moment that most defines you in your life. For those who are brave, it could be a negative one that has defined you. Nobody is pushed into exposing anything.
A student told of a presentation in a foreign language that the whole class applauded, and how proud and defined it made her feel.
I said that a piece of paper from such a moment becomes symbolic and gains consciousness, because we attach consciousness to objects that represent things, as flags do.

I said that we carry a memory like that and may spend a life looking for approval. I said we do not tend to think about these things and sweep them under the rug, but they surface, in a lack of confidence or in a five-second decision.
If a moment is heavy, a person with the right training is the right place to take it. You do not have to share it here.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one moment that defines you, if you want to.
Write what you took from it.
Write the object that stands for it.
Write where it shows up in your day.
Write who you could talk to if it is heavy.

check.q: What did I ask each person for?
choices: The moment that most defines them

check.q: What did I say objects can have?
What did I say happens to what we sweep under the rug?

recap: Name a moment that defines you. Notice where it shows up.
